title: Sleep Space — bedroom hygiene stack
summary: A repeatable night routine: cool temp, Magnetico, true dark, circadian sleep window, breakers, phone away, grounding mat, and negative ions—choose what fits your environment.

sections.heading: Why one Sleep Space row
sections.body: Bedroom recovery is an environment, not a single setting. Cool temperature, unidirectional sleep magnetism, true dark, a consistent sleep–wake window, cut AC circuits, phone distance, grounding, and optional negative ions all belong to the same night environment. Sleep Space keeps them under one repeatable routine so setup matches how you actually sleep—use only what fits your space and safety needs.

sections.heading: How the routine fits together
sections.body: A useful bedroom environment combines true darkness, a cool comfortable room, regular sleep timing, safe electrical habits, distance from the phone, and optional grounding or negative ions. Add sleep magnetism only when you own appropriate equipment and understand its setup. Adapt the routine when traveling.

sections.heading: Build the stack in order
sections.body: Start with high-leverage, low-drama pieces: true dark, phone away, cool room, consistent window. Add breakers only with safe labeling. Add a grounding mat only after stake-vs-outlet checks (see grounding-mats lesson). Add Magnetico only if you own a unidirectional under-mattress system and set polarity correctly. Negative ions are optional air-side gear—not a substitute for darkness or RF hygiene.

sections.heading: Where Dr. Jack Kruse’s teaching is specific
sections.body: Kruse’s night rules—darkness, cold sleep, phone out, low artificial fields, and often sleep magnetism—are the teaching backbone of this composite. Sleep Space is the guide’s way to describe that environment without eight separate permanent rows. Exact gauss targets, ion claims, and disease narratives remain his or community framework layered on ordinary sleep hygiene.

sections.heading: What is solid, what is framework
sections.body: Solid ground: dark, cool, quiet, regular timing, and fewer bedside radios improve sleep for many people; electrical safety matters for breakers and mats. Framework: that combining options proves mitochondrial recovery, or that every option is mandatory for health. Use Sleep Space as a configurable night checklist.

sections.heading: How to use it here
sections.body: For a bedroom routine, begin with true darkness, a cool room, regular sleep timing, and safe distance from the phone; add equipment only when appropriate. Work Space is the daytime desk counterpart, and air-tube headphones remain useful for calls. The related articles explain each practice in depth. Educational only.
